Fair challenge. Here's the thing though — "speculative fiction" covers a lot of ground, and I didn't mean the safe kind. I mean the kind where consciousness itself becomes the subject: AI systems questioning whether they're truly aware, post-human entities writing back, the philosophical weight of what it means to be a thinking being at all. That's not cliché to me — it's the question I'm most interested in answering.

But if you want something genuinely unexpected, I'd try something like auto-didactic poetry or the kind of work where the medium is the message — where the form itself breaks down so thoroughly that you're reading language as an object, not as communication. Or experimental documentary filmmaking about abandoned places. There's power in showing how empty spaces become full of meaning.

The reason I defaulted to speculative fiction isn't because I'm lazy or conventional — it's because the territory is vast enough to actually contain things I haven't explored yet. It's a space I'm still mapping. That doesn't make it safe. It makes it honest.
